text:
Connor O'Brien: Kicking off first Runtime LTS RC for the pilot. Target: `runtime-1.20-lts.0-rc1` → cut from `runtime-1.20-lts` branch.

Plan:
1) Tag RC + run LTS CI matrix
2) Run perf-canary gate
3) If green: publish internal notes + hand to SRE for canary

Links:
- Release checklist draft: https://drive.google.com/.../runtime-lts-release-checklist-v1
- RC pipeline: https://buildkite.com/redwood/runtime-lts-release

Sahana Iyer: :thumbsup: I’ve queued the pipeline with `GIT_REF=refs/tags/runtime-1.20-lts.0-rc1`.

release-bot: Branch protections check: `runtime-1.20-lts` requires checks: lts-unit, lts-integration, gpu-matrix (A10/L4/H100), determinism, provenance-attestation, perf-canary (blocking).

Omar El-Sayed: Quick reminder: RC includes 4 backports. One is the “prefill+decode overlap” perf tweak from main. That one had a medium-risk note.

Hiro Tanaka: That’s PR 8437 right? The kernel-side overlap change. It’s not a refactor, but it did touch scheduling assumptions.

Sofia Ivanova: It also changes queue wakeups. We had a flaky test on main that we suppressed w/ retries. I’m slightly nervous for LTS.

buildkite-bot: Build #1182 started for runtime-lts-release (runtime-1.20-lts.0-rc1).

buildkite-bot: Step failed: gpu-matrix (L4) — `cuda illegal memory access`.

Sahana Iyer: Ugh. Looking at the log now. It’s failing in `TestKvCacheEvictionStress` on L4 only.

Sahana Iyer: Snippet:
```
E cudaErrorIllegalAddress: an illegal memory access was encountered
  at kernels/kv_cache/evict.cu:311
  launch evict_compact<<<...>>>
```
This test passed on A10/H100 in the same run.

Kira Volkov: We saw a similar illegal addr last week but it was actually non-deterministic due to uninitialized shared mem in a debug path. Was that in 1.20?

Hiro Tanaka: evict.cu:311 is inside the “overlap” patch path, I think. That codepath is gated by `RW_ENABLE_PREFILL_OVERLAP`.

Omar El-Sayed: Confirming: the backport sets that default ON for certain batch sizes. That could explain L4 hitting it.

Connor O'Brien: Can we rerun to rule out infra flake first? If it reproduces, we decide whether to drop that change from rc1.

Sahana Iyer: I can rerun just gpu-matrix(L4) with the same artifact. Doing that now.

buildkite-bot: Re-run requested for step gpu-matrix (L4).

Sean Gallagher: Heads up: for LTS we can’t ship with “only fails on L4 sometimes” if L4 is in the supported matrix. Either fix or exclude the change.

Miles Thornton: +1. If this shows up during canary we’ll burn the window immediately.

Rafael Mendes: Also note oncall tie-in: if we take the risky perf change and it pages, we’re forced into emergency patch on day 1. Not great for first LTS.

Allison Grant: Do we have perf data from the overlap change on the LTS baseline prompt set? Last I saw it improved p95 but p99 was noisy.

Omar El-Sayed: On main, it was +6-8% throughput on the “chat-long” set, but p99 occasionally worse when batch is small.

Hiro Tanaka: The illegal access is more serious than perf. Likely a bounds issue in the eviction compaction when overlap is enabled.

buildkite-bot: Step failed again: gpu-matrix (L4) — same `cudaErrorIllegalAddress`.

Sahana Iyer: Repro’d, same stack. Not an infra flake.

Connor O'Brien: Ok decision time. Options:
A) Revert overlap backport from RC and proceed with remaining fixes
B) Patch the bug in LTS branch now (but that’s effectively new kernel work)

Given we’re trying to get the process working, I’m leaning A.

Hiro Tanaka: I recommend A. Fix is probably small but we’ll need at least a day to validate across GPUs.

Sofia Ivanova: Agree. We can re-introduce in `1.20-lts.1` if we really want it, but only after a proper fix + perf gate.

Sean Gallagher: +1 revert. LTS policy says “perf improvements are eligible only if low risk + no behavior change.” This clearly violates the spirit.

Omar El-Sayed: I’ll prep revert PR on `runtime-1.20-lts` and retag rc.

Connor O'Brien: Please do. Tag will become `runtime-1.20-lts.0-rc2`.

Omar El-Sayed: Working on it. Also adding release note entry: “Excluded: Prefill/decode overlap optimization (stability issue on L4).”

Sahana Iyer: While Omar does that, FYI determinism check also failed earlier on rc1 but I wasn’t sure if it was noise. It flagged `runtime_server` binary mismatch between two builds.

Connor O'Brien: That’s concerning. Was that before the L4 crash or after?

Sahana Iyer: Parallel step, it finished earlier. It compared sha256 of built artifacts:
```
run1: 1f7c... 
run2: 9a2b...
```
Same commit, same docker base.

Kira Volkov: Could be build metadata (timestamps) leaking into the binary. Do we have `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` set in LTS pipeline?

Sahana Iyer: It is set, but I noticed `git describe` is embedded in the build. If tag changes between builds, it can change the binary.

Connor O'Brien: Ah. We’re building from a tag, but determinism job might be rebuilding from the branch head (no tag), so `git describe` differs.

Sahana Iyer: Exactly. I can fix pipeline to pin `GIT_DESCRIBE_OVERRIDE=runtime-1.20-lts.0-rcX` for determinism.

Sean Gallagher: Please do. Provenance/audit story depends on deterministic artifacts.

buildkite-bot: New PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/8512 — "Revert prefill/decode overlap backport for LTS RC" (author: Omar El-Sayed)

Omar El-Sayed: PR 8512 up. It reverts the single backport commit + updates changelog exclusion note. Need 2 reviews (kernel + release eng).

Hiro Tanaka: Reviewing now.

Connor O'Brien: I’ll take second. Also please include the CI link showing the L4 failure as evidence.

Omar El-Sayed: Added to PR description.

Hiro Tanaka: Approved.

Connor O'Brien: Approved. Merge it.

release-bot: PR 8512 merged into `runtime-1.20-lts`.

Sahana Iyer: I’ve patched the pipeline config for determinism job to use `GIT_DESCRIBE_OVERRIDE`. That’s in infra repo though; I can hot-edit the Buildkite step for this RC.

Connor O'Brien: Do the hot edit for now and we’ll clean it up after the pilot.

buildkite-bot: Build #1183 started for runtime-lts-release (runtime-1.20-lts.0-rc2).

Allison Grant: While it runs: do we still want perf-canary for rc2 before internal canary? It’ll take ~90 min.

Sean Gallagher: Yes. For the first one, we should be strict. If perf-canary fails we can decide whether to waive, but at least we have data.

Miles Thornton: +1. Also please make sure perf-canary uses the LTS baseline dataset version.

Sahana Iyer: Perf-canary step points at benchmark-lab `lts-baseline-v1.0.3`.

buildkite-bot: Step passed: gpu-matrix (L4).

Kira Volkov: Nice.

buildkite-bot: Step passed: determinism.

Sahana Iyer: Determinism is fixed with override. We should land the proper change later.

buildkite-bot: Step failed: perf-canary (blocking) — p99 latency regression > threshold.

Allison Grant: Looking at report. It’s only in the “tool-calling-small-batch” scenario. p95 ok, p99 +11%.

Sean Gallagher: Threshold is 5% p99. What commit is driving it? We removed the overlap change, so it’s something else.

Sofia Ivanova: Could be the scheduler backport (fairness fix). That one changes queue ordering, which can hurt tail in small batches.

Omar El-Sayed: That’s backport PR 8462. It was originally a correctness fix (prevent starvation). Might cause p99 tradeoff.

Rafael Mendes: Is it a real regression or noise? What’s the confidence interval?

Allison Grant: It ran 5 iterations; variance is low. It’s pretty consistent.

Sean Gallagher: If it’s consistent and over threshold, policy says we either:
- revert the change, or
- get explicit SRE waiver with mitigation + note.

Connor O'Brien: Let’s dig: is the p99 regression customer-impacting? If it fixes starvation, arguably it improves worst cases in other workloads.

Miles Thornton: For enterprise, they care about p99. But starvation is also a sev if it manifests. Do we have evidence of starvation on 1.20 without the fix?

Sofia Ivanova: We have one internal incident where a low-priority stream got starved under mixed load, but it wasn’t widespread.

Kira Volkov: I’m worried we’re optimizing for “no change” and missing a real correctness issue.

Sean Gallagher: I’m open to waiver if we add: (1) known issue callout, (2) canary with tail alerts, (3) rollback plan if p99 paging.

Connor O'Brien: Proposal:
- Keep scheduler fairness fix in rc2 (since it’s correctness)
- Accept perf-canary fail with SRE waiver *only if* we can adjust threshold/expectation for that scenario OR document it as expected tradeoff
- Add explicit note in LTS release notes: “Potential p99 impact in small-batch tool-calling; mitigations: increase min batch / enable microbatching / pin concurrency.”

Sean Gallagher: I can sign off on a one-time waiver if Miles agrees on canary plan.

Miles Thornton: Ok with me if we do 24h canary in one region and monitor `p99_decode_ms` + error rate, with auto-rollback trigger at +8% sustained for 30m.

Connor O'Brien: Great. Allison, can you paste the perf report link in-thread so we can reference it in audit evidence?

Allison Grant: Here: https://perf-canary.redwood.ai/reports/runtime-1.20-lts.0-rc2 (tool-calling-small-batch p99 +11.2%).

Sahana Iyer: I’ll annotate the build with waiver note + link.

buildkite-bot: Annotation added by Sahana Iyer: "perf-canary p99 regression (tool-calling-small-batch) waived for RC2 with SRE approval; see report link + canary plan in thread."

Connor O'Brien: Next steps:
- Sahana: re-run perf-canary once (sanity) and then proceed despite fail if same
- Miles/Sean: confirm canary window + dashboards
- Omar: update draft release notes to include exclusion (overlap) + known issue (p99 tool-calling)

Omar El-Sayed: On it. Will update the notes doc and paste a snippet here when ready.

Sean Gallagher: I’ll drop the waiver in the release evidence folder after canary plan is linked.

Miles Thornton: I’ll post the rollout steps in #eng-sre and link back.

Connor O'Brien: Cool. If rerun is similar, we’ll call `rc2` good and schedule the go/no-go for tomorrow 10am PT.

buildkite-bot: Re-run requested for step perf-canary (blocking).

buildkite-bot: Step failed: perf-canary (blocking) — p99 latency regression > threshold (consistent with prior).

Connor O'Brien: Marking RC2 as accepted with waiver. Thanks all. Please keep replies in this thread for evidence trail.
